subject: mathematics_1b
question_text: Find the points on the line 3x−4y−1=0 which are at a distance of 5 units from the point (3,2).

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1B (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.63 — SAQ chapter 9 The Straight Line, answer 59, on a ★★★ SSP (Super Scoring Page). Printed appearances: AP M-16 · AP 15. THE MARK SPLIT 1+1+2 IS THE BOOK'S: answer 59 on book p.63 is the ONE answer in this unit's SAQ chapter that carries printed margin tags — '1 Mark' beside the slope-to-cos-and-sin step, '1 Mark' beside the parametric-point line, and '2 Marks' beside the two required points. Paper position: Maths-1B Section B runs Q11-Q17 at 4 marks each, answer any 5 of 7. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. NOTE: The Straight Line is the FIRST Maths-1B unit to occupy ALL THREE sections of the paper — the book's IPE Blue Print (book p.3) gives it 2+2 marks in Section A, 4 in Section B and 7 in Section C, 15 in all, tying Differentiation as the highest-scoring unit on the paper. It therefore has three separate chapters in this book: LAQ chapter 1 (book pp.14-18), SAQ chapter 9 (pp.61-64) and VSAQ chapter 14 (pp.79-82). All three boundaries were walked: p.19 opens Pair of Straight Lines, p.65 opens Limits & Continuity, and p.83 opens 3-D Coordinates. The book's separate STAR QUESTIONS PLUS bank (pp.104-108) contributes three more, answers 182-184, authored here as sqp1-sqp3.

recall_prompt: Say how you would solve this — say what you convert the slope into, and why there are two answers.

steps.label: Slope to cosθ and sinθ
steps.margin_note: First mark, printed in the book's margin. The parametric form needs cosθ and sinθ, not the slope — and from tanθ = 3/4 the 3-4-5 triangle gives both at once with no calculator.
steps.memory_tip: The parametric form needs cos θ and sin θ. From tan θ = 3/4 the 3-4-5 triangle gives both with no calculator.

recall.must_convey: That the slope 3/4 is converted to cosθ = 4/5 and sinθ = 3/5.
accept: the slope is three by four so cos theta is four fifths and sin theta is three fifths
tan theta equals three over four gives the three four five triangle
convert the slope into cos and sin
slope nunchi cos theta sin theta teesukovali
cos is four by five and sin is three by five

steps.why: tanθ = 3/4 means the right triangle has sides 3 and 4 and hypotenuse 5, so cosθ and sinθ come out exactly — this is why the question chose these numbers.
common_mistakes: Taking cosθ = 3/5 and sinθ = 4/5, with the two swapped.
Trying to find θ itself instead of just its cosine and sine.

steps.label: Write the parametric point
steps.margin_note: Second mark, also printed. The two points sit at distance 5 on EITHER side of (3,2), so the ± is written into the parametric form from the start.
steps.memory_tip: The two points sit on EITHER side, so write the ± into the parametric form from the start.
lines: Required points (x, y) = (x₁ ± r cosθ, y₁ ± r sinθ)

recall.must_convey: That the required points are (x₁ ± r cosθ, y₁ ± r sinθ) = (3 ± 4, 2 ± 3).
accept: the points are three plus or minus four comma two plus or minus three
use the parametric form with plus or minus because there are two points
distance five each way along the line
rendu vaipula unnaayi kabatti plus or minus
write the parametric point with plus or minus r

steps.why: A given distance from a point along a line is reached in BOTH directions, so the ± is not optional — it is what produces the two points the question asks for.
common_mistakes: Using only + and finding one point.
Multiplying 5 by cosθ and sinθ the wrong way round.

steps.label: State both required points
steps.margin_note: The last two marks, printed as '2 Marks'. Take the signs TOGETHER — both plus, then both minus. Mixing them gives points that are not on the line.
steps.memory_tip: Take the signs TOGETHER — both plus, then both minus. Mixing them gives points off the line.

recall.must_convey: That the two points are (7, 5) and (−1, −1).
accept: the points are seven comma five and minus one comma minus one
take both plus signs together then both minus signs together
rendu points seven five and minus one minus one

steps.why: The ± must be taken consistently in both coordinates, because they describe one step of length 5 in one direction — mixing the signs steps sideways off the line.
common_mistakes: Mixing the signs and reporting (7, −1) or (−1, 5).
Reporting only one of the two points.
